body.x: CIT Co., Ltd. (CEO Seung Jeong) participated in the Global Media Online Meetup on July 31, hosted in collaboration with U.S. tech media outlet Geekspin and Korean startups.

The event, co-hosted by AVING News and Geekspin, aims to introduce Korean startups and their technologies to global media, spotlighting CES 2026 Innovation Award applicants and paving the way for international business expansion.

Founded in 2023, Copper Innovation Technology (CIT) develops advanced electronic materials for ultra-high-speed communication. Its substrates support both wired (up to 10Gbps) and wireless (1–100GHz) transmission and offer low signal loss. Its ultra-thin copper film, made from recycled waste wire, is just 300nm thick—50 times thinner than conventional 15μm copper foil—and provides equal performance, demonstrating both technological innovation and environmental sustainability.

CIT’s core technology, Atomic Sputter Epitaxy (ASE), enables uniform deposition of copper atoms without adhesive, arranging a trillion atoms per cubic centimeter. This precise process is key to applications like transparent antennas and displays. It was published in “Nature” in 2022 and 2023, validating the company’s global R&D excellence.

CIT has already achieved localization of communication substrates, reducing foreign dependence. Within six months of founding, it attracted KRW 1.1 billion in seed investment with a KRW 5.6 billion valuation, followed by KRW 2 billion at a KRW 14 billion valuation in 2024. Despite operating only a pilot line, CIT has formed partnerships with global players like Parallel Wireless (USA) and Huawei (China). In February 2024, it signed an MOU with Harvard Medical School and Massachusetts General Hospital for joint research in bio-recognition and medical materials.

The company also joined MWC 2024, engaging European medical and healthcare companies, and secured further partnerships at CES and MWC 2025. Its transparent antenna earned a CES 2025 Innovation Award in the Vehicle Tech & Advanced Mobility category.

body.x: With its CES 2025 Innovation Award, CIT strengthened trust with global material companies like Japan’s Asahi Glass (AGC), connected with new buyers and partners, and enhanced brand credibility.

CIT now aims to win the CES 2026 Innovation Award with its new product, CuFlat-PKGCore™—a next-generation board for AI accelerators. Developed using CIT’s proprietary ASE technology, the product deposits ultra-flat copper on glass substrates without seed layers, electroless plating, or CMP—replacing three or more complex steps with a single process.

The board achieves under-4nm surface roughness, 7% lower surface resistance, and uniform deposition on high-aspect-ratio glass (up to 8:1). It retains stability up to 250°C without oxidation—2.5 times higher than conventional copper’s 100°C limit—preventing performance degradation in AI accelerators.

The ASE technology’s ultra-precise atomic alignment maximizes board design flexibility. CuFlat-PKGCore™ supports multiple glass types (borosilicate, alkali-free) and applies to both core and interposer substrates. It also offers design freedom that allows packaging engineers to realize their intent fully.

Additionally, the product produces zero chemical wastewater and uses 100% recycled copper, reducing its carbon footprint by over 95% (from 3.75 tons to 0.0175 tons). Its high heat and oxidation resistance also help lower energy use for data center cooling, which typically consumes 40% of a center’s power. CuFlat-PKGCore™ enables high performance in 20°C environments with minimal cooling, offering both efficiency and sustainability.

body.x: Looking ahead, CIT plans to collaborate with major semiconductor packaging firms in the U.S., Europe, and Asia—key markets for AI and HPC. Targets include Intel, AMD, NVIDIA, Samsung Electro-Mechanics, and Absolics, aiming for joint development and commercialization of glass substrate technologies.

CIT will also participate in InnoEX 2025 (Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, August 21–22) and SWITCH/SLINGSHOT (Singapore, October), reinforcing its presence in Southeast Asia and the Asia-Pacific region. It will return to CES and MWC in 2026 to deepen ties with global clients and attract investment. With strategic exhibitions and partnerships, CIT aims to expand its presence in the worldwide supply chain.

CIT emphasized that while copper-deposited glass substrates are its core business, the technology has broad applications across industries. Sectors like autonomous driving, smartphones, and 6G demand components that remain stable in outdoor or high-heat conditions. CIT’s copper layer resists oxidation up to 250°C and enables ultra-flat circuit surfaces for faster processing—perfectly aligning with high-speed, high-volume data transmission needs.

“Our goal is to become the leading copper deposition company for glass substrates by collaborating with global semiconductor and equipment firms on joint development projects,” said a CIT spokesperson.

Founded in 2017, Geekspin is a U.S.-based tech media outlet led by Helena Stone, a product expert featured on MSNBC, Wired, ABC News, TIME, and Woman’s Day. The publication covers CES annually, highlighting emerging technologies from around the world.
